text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we standardize on QUIC (HTTP/3) as the primary transport for control‑plane tunnels between customer agents and the private control plane. TL;DR: multiplexed streams, quicker reconnects, less HOL blocking. Thoughts?

smita: Interesting. Biggest immediate worry is UDP being blocked in corporate networks. Do we have a sensible fallback plan?

jorge: UDP filtering is real. We saw corporate proxies drop UDP or force UDP->TCP. QUIC helps a lot for lots of small independent streams (health, metrics, commands). But agree we need a TCP/TLS fallback.

morgan: Enterprise/security note: many customers use TLS interceptors (proxy with MITM). QUIC/TLS is opaque to those tools. How do we support customers that require inspection?

alex: Plan A: default QUIC + mTLS using client certs. Plan B: fallback to TCP/TLS when we detect proxy/downstream that blocks UDP or requires interception. We could make the agent prefer QUIC but allow an override in config.

nate: What about perf numbers? connection setup latency, CPU cost for QUIC vs TCP+TLS (especially with rehandshake scenarios)? We should spike.

smita: We already ran a micro-spike last quarter. Quick notes: QUIC cold handshake ~20–40ms on average on noisy networks vs TCP+TLS often >100ms because of SYN/ACK+TLS RTTs. CPU cost per handshake slightly higher for QUIC but overall lower due to fewer rehandshakes and session resumption. Will pull logs.

smita: Example agent config draft we used in tests:

```
agent.transport: quic
agent.quic: 
  enabled: true
  idle_timeout: 60s
  max_concurrent_streams: 128
  mtu: 1200  # avoid fragmentation on middleboxes
  resumption: true
agent.fallback: tcp_tls  # try QUIC then TCP/TLS
```

morgan: Note re MTU — fragmentation over UDP causes issues on some egress paths. keep mtu <= 1200 and implement PMTU probing/respect Fallback.

jorge: Also think about session resumption and connection pinning for mobile agents. QUIC resumption (0-RTT in some libs) helps mobile/spotty networks dramatically.

alex: Good. A few RFC decision points for follow-up: 1) Default transport: QUIC with TCP/TLS fallback vs opt-in QUIC only; 2) How to detect UDP-blocking proxies reliably (port probe? failure heuristics?); 3) MTU default and fragmentation handling; 4) mTLS + SPNEGO/enterprise inspection story (document constraints); 5) rollout plan: spike -> canary Dedicated -> Private installs; 6) cert rotation over QUIC (SPIRE integration).

nate: I'll partner with @smita for a 2-week spike. Deliverables: perf matrix (handshake RTT, p50/p95 tail for control RPCs), CPU/memory delta, failure modes across corp proxies (Blue Coat, Palo Alto, ZScaler).

smita: Sounds good — starting Monday. Will create reproducible test harness (kubernetes pods simulating agent, and control plane relay) and a small script to flip transports.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-3421: "QUIC control-plane tunnel spike — perf and proxy compatibility" and linked to arch board.

morgan: Also flag Legal/security: QUIC libs sometimes include non-US crypto features. Need export-compliance sign-off if we ship agent bundles with certain ciphers.

alex: Noted. I'll ping Legal and Security.

jorge: One more subtlety — observability. With QUIC multiplexing we need per-stream tracing context and per-stream metrics so we can still attribute latency/cost to routes. Otherwise dashboards will look different.

smita: We'll instrument per-stream histograms. For traces we'll propagate traceparent in headers on each stream.

alex: Great. If the spike is positive, proposal is to enable QUIC by default in Hosted/Dedicated and opt-in for Private until we have documented inspection constraints. Canary first.

nate: I'm in. Will add test matrix to INFRA-3421.

alex: Thanks all. We'll sync after the spike for an RFC update. :thumbsup:
